title: Execution of decree - why winning a case is only half the battle
p1:
Winning a case feels like the finish line. But for many people, the real challenge begins after the judgment is delivered.

A court order may declare your rights, but it does not automatically put the result into your hands.
p2:
Many assume that once a judge rules in their favour, the other side must immediately comply. The lesser-known reality is that a separate legal process called execution may be needed to enforce that decision.

Execution is the stage where the court helps the successful party actually receive what was awarded — whether it is money, property, or another remedy.
p3:
This is why a favourable judgment and actual relief are two different things. A person can win a case on paper but still face delays if the decree is not properly enforced.

The practical lesson: a legal victory is valuable only when it can be translated into action. Knowing the steps after a judgment can be just as important as proving your case in court.
conclusion: Have you ever wondered why some people win court cases but still struggle to get the final outcome? What do you think is the biggest challenge after a judgment is passed?
